million and milliard take -s only when greater than un
million and milliard are nouns and require de before a following noun (deux millions de personnes)

proposals.entity_key: Possessive adjectives agree with the noun they modify
value: Agreement is with the possessed noun, not with the possessor
son/sa/ses can mean his, her, or its; only context disambiguates
The masculine forms mon, ton, son replace ma, ta, sa before feminine nouns beginning with a vowel or mute h

evidence.notes: First two entries follow from the rule and its trap; the third is the rule's stated exception phrased as a limit.

proposals.entity_key: Possessive pronouns replace noun + possessive adjective
value: Always preceded by a definite article (le, la, les)
Agreement is with the replaced noun, not with the possessor
à and de contract with the article (au mien, du mien); à le mien and de le mien do not occur

evidence.notes: Derived from the stated condition, agreement rule, and contraction exception.

proposals.entity_key: Possessive pronouns with aussi and non plus

non plus is used only in negative contexts

proposals.entity_key: Preposition with countries: en, au, aux
value: à is not used directly before a country name
en is used only for feminine countries and masculine countries beginning with a vowel
Cities take à, not en or au

evidence.notes: First two entries come from the formation and the stated trap; the city contrast is standard usage.

proposals.entity_key: Preposition with islands: à, aux, en
value: Usage varies by island, so the pattern is not fully predictable
The exceptions en Haïti, en Martinique, en Guadeloupe do not take à
Plural island groups take aux, not à

evidence.notes: Derived from the rule's note on varying usage and its listed exceptions.

proposals.entity_key: Preposition with states/provinces: en, au, dans le
value: en applies only to feminine states/provinces or masculine ones beginning with a vowel
au applies to masculine states, not to feminine ones
dans le is used with masculine states beginning with a consonant instead of au

evidence.notes: All three entries follow from the source text's stated variation patterns.
